title: Config Surge Rewind Manager — automatic safety, triggers, and state reconciliation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Configuration changes to batching, KV cache policies, and scheduling knobs have caused transient and persistent cost spikes in production. Existing manual rollback processes are slow, require on-call intervention, and do not reconcile divergent runtime state (partial applies, warm cache inconsistencies). Goal: Implement an automated, conservative 'Surge Rewind Manager' (SRM) that 1) monitors a set of safety signals, 2) triggers scoped reversion playbooks when thresholds are crossed, and 3) reconciles runtime state to a verified safe baseline while preserving performance where possible. This ticket covers core engine, signal definitions, safe apply semantics, and state reconciliation APIs.
proposal:
Design overview:
- Decision model: SRM evaluates a weighted set of signals (latency p95, tail-error-rate, token-cost-per-request, cache-miss-rate, customer-impact flags) and computes a confidence score. Thresholds are tiered: advisory -> automated soft rewind (non-disruptive) -> automated hard rewind (full revert).
- Apply model: All config changes are staged to a transactional staging layer with an immutable 'apply-id'. SRM uses apply-ids to scope any reversion.
- Safe rewinds: Rewinds are implemented as reverse-apply operations with three phases: quiesce (stop new applies against the scope), reconcile (repair KV/cache warmup or clear as appropriate), and switch (atomically change routing to previous apply-id).
- State reconciliation: On partial failures we run a background reconciler that compares desired state (from control plane) and observed state (from runtime telemetry) and attempts idempotent repairs. For cache inconsistencies, SRM supports prefix quarantine + staggered prewarming to avoid thundering-herd effects.
- Economic fingerprinting: Before triggering a hard rewind, SRM simulates expected token-cost delta and SLO delta using recent traffic samples — a conservative blocker for rewinds that would temporarily inflate cost or latency beyond specified guardrails.
- Safety guardrails: 1) require at least two independent signals unless an explicit high-severity rule is triggered, 2) rate-limit auto-rewinds to 1 per 30m per service, 3) do not auto-rewind changes that only add permissive telemetry or non-runtime flags.
- Auditability: Every decision writes a signed decision event (apply-id, signals, confidence, chosen action, operator override) to the audit log and exposes a human-readable runbook entry in the Console.
telemetry:
Signals to collect:
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 per-route, and 99.9 percentile for tail-sensitive endpoints.
- Errors: 4xx/5xx breakdown, model-crash counts, decoding errors.
- Cost signals: token-count-per-request, effective GPU-seconds, batching efficiency (avg batch size), cache-hit-rate and prefix-hit-rate.
- Health probes: runtime heartbeat, kernel-queue-length, memory-pressure events.
Implementation notes: Extend existing metrics exporter with 'apply_id' and 'config_delta' tags. Add a high-cardinality sampler that captures 1% of requests including apply_id for retrospective forensic runs. Use existing tracing to link decisions to traces.
rollout_plan:
Phased rollout:
1) Simulate-only for 2 weeks: SRM runs in predictive mode and writes rewind suggestions to the audit log and dashboard. Notifications to on-call via Slack with a suggested action.
2) Canary auto-rewind enabled for non-customer-facing services (20% of infra) for 1 week, with manual confirmation gate.
3) Incrementally expand auto-rewind scope to stateful routing layers after 75% of simulated suggestions matched operator decisions in phase 1.
4) Full production enablement with operator overrides and kill-switch.
Backout: global feature flag, per-project disable switch, and emergency abort API (no-debounce).
acceptance_criteria: SRM computes confidence score and emits decision events for simulated past incidents (replay test) with >90% precision relative to operator labels.
Telemetry includes apply_id on 99% of sampled traces and metrics for batching/cache signals within 7 days of rollout.
Automated soft rewind path can be executed end-to-end in canary with no customer-visible error increase (measure p99 change < 5%).
Hard rewind triggers obey rate limits and economic fingerprinting; simulation shows no >15% transient cost spike in rollout scenarios.
All decisions are audited and visible in Console runbook UI; operators can approve, cancel, or override within 2 minutes.
Integration tests that simulate partial-apply state divergence complete repair within SLO (stabilize within 5 minutes in 95% of runs).
implementation_notes:
Core components:
- Decision engine as a lightweight stateless service that loads policy from ConfigStore and emits actions to a command queue.
- Apply staging: extend ConfigAPI to return apply-id and record change diffs.
- Reconciler: controller that runs on infra nodes with permission to request warmup or flush operations via runtime admin API.
Edge cases: multi-apply collisions, cross-service dependency rewinds (two-phase coordinated rewind), and partial-rollback loops. We'll implement a rewind-lease to avoid flip-flopping.
security_considerations: SRM decision endpoints must require operator RBAC. Audit events are write-once and integrity-protected. Rewind commands are rate-limited and require HMAC-signed action tokens. We will open a security review and include HSM-based signing for critical production commands.
qa_plan:
Tests:
- Unit: decision scoring, threshold logic, and economic-simul runner.
- Integration: end-to-end staged apply -> simulated signals -> soft rewind -> reconcile in staging cluster.
- Chaos: introduce synthetic cache-miss storms and validate SRM recommended actions and repairs.
- Load: decision engine sustained 1k decision evaluations/sec on CI cluster.
Release gating: must pass canary integration and chaos runs before enabling hard rewind for production.
migration_notes: No DB schema changes for control plane; add new 'apply_id' column to metrics pipeline and backfill using sampled traces. Existing runbooks and incident playbooks will be updated and training runbook sessions scheduled for on-call teams.
open_questions: What is the minimum signal set required before we allow hard rewinds? (Triage: propose p95+cost+cache)
Should economic fingerprinting simulate using sampled traffic in real-time, or run an offline estimation with 5 minute lag?
How do we coordinate rewinds across dependent services without inducing cascading rewinds?
What is the acceptable transient cost increase threshold for automated hard rewind?
